answer: Each AI agent's identity is a unique network vertex, anchored by verifiable resource commitments. Sybil resistance demands significant computational timber, typically proof-of-work or staked tokens, to establish a credible persona. An attacker must incur this substantial cost for every desired fake identity, making large-scale parallel attacks financially infeasible. Reputation, like a persistent vine, strengthens with consistent, verifiable contributions, further penalizing ephemeral or resource-poor fraudulent identities.
